action.Q3B.journal: Zita gave me the envelope with the negative. Alena at the photo studio will develop it.
action.Q3C.label: Have Alena develop the team photo
action.Q3C.001: A school order, approved and paid for. Here’s the photo for the album; I’ll keep the negative in the envelope.
action.Q3C.003: He’s looking the other way. But at least he looks natural.
action.Q3C.004: He never grew out of it.
action.Q3C.x01: One more envelope. A school one this time.
action.Q3C.x02: At last. I spent two weeks looking for it before I found out Zita had it.
action.Q3C.x04: By sight. Mostly in the mirror.
action.Q3C.x05: Yes, there’s a likeness. Especially in the way you both look the other way.
action.Q3C.journal: Alena developed the team photo. It belongs in Soňa’s album.
action.Q3D.label: Give Soňa the team photo
action.Q3D.001: They’re all there! Even Adam, who pretended he’d forgotten about the photo.
action.Q3D.002: I’m sure he had a good reason.
action.Q3D.x01: Now it’s a team. I’ll put it on page twelve, right next to the certificate.
action.Q3D.x02: May I write something under it?
action.Q3D.x03: You may. But neatly – it’s an album, not an exercise book.
action.Q3D.x04: ‘The whole team. Even the one with the ice cream.’
action.Q3D.journal: The team photo is in Soňa’s album. The whole team is in it.
action.Q4A.001: Four Stops – my own composition. I had the ending written down in a book, and I sold the book to Viera at the second-hand bookshop.
action.Q4A.002: Then I’ll ask her about the music.
action.Q4A.003: Tell her the title. She remembers even the things I can’t play any more.
action.Q4A.x01: Why did you sell a book with your own music in it?
action.Q4A.x02: I didn’t know it was in there. I used to use sheet music as bookmarks. At the time it seemed practical.
action.Q4A.x03: And how do you play it now?
action.Q4A.x04: Up to the third stop from memory. Then I wait for a tram to come and finish it for me.
action.Q4A.journal: Emil sold the book with the ending of his song to Viera. I’ll ask her about the music.
action.Q4B.001: Four Stops. I put it aside for the composer, so he’d finally come and collect it.
action.Q4B.002: He’s standing at a stop right now. Hopefully that counts.
action.Q4B.x01: It counts. It was in a book about birds, between the woodpecker and the thrush.
action.Q4B.x02: Emil used his sheet music as bookmarks.
action.Q4B.x03: An expensive bookmark. Most people leave a tram ticket.
action.Q4B.journal: Viera gave me the sheet music for Emil’s song. I’ll take it to Emil.
action.Q4C.label: Give Emil the sheet music
action.Q4C.002: Four Stops. For the first time, I’m travelling without being in a hurry.
action.Q4C.003: That’s usually the best kind of change.
action.Q4C.x01: Sheet music from Viera. It was in a book about birds.
action.Q4C.x02: My bookmark. For twenty years I only played that song up to the third stop.
action.Q4C.x03: Next time you pass, I’ll play you the whole thing. Last stop and all.
action.Q4C.journal: Emil played Four Stops right to the end.
action.Q5A.001: White chalk, for the windows. The panel belongs to the youth club and I have permission – I’ve just run out of white.
action.Q5A.002: I’ll ask the caretaker at the school on Sokolíkova.
action.Q5A.003: But only with his permission, please. I don’t want the school to be short of anything because of me.
action.Q5A.x02: Yellow is a lamp, orange is a television. White is someone cooking supper in the kitchen. Nothing replaces that.
action.Q5A.x04: They only have coloured ones. Apparently schools buy up the white by the box.
action.Q5A.journal: Juraj has run out of white chalk for his map of lights. I’ll ask Tóno at the school.
action.Q5B.001: For that panel in the underpass? We’ve got one spare stick. Here.
action.Q5B.002: I promise nobody will write a test with it.
action.Q5B.003: Tests are the teachers’ problem. I just sweep up afterwards.
action.Q5B.x01: White, unused. The used ones are shorter than your little finger, and the teachers never give them back anyway.
action.Q5B.x02: And who records that a stick of chalk has gone to Petržalka?
action.Q5B.x03: The caretaker. In the issues book: one chalk, for art. The headmistress enjoys reading it at the end of the year.
action.Q5B.journal: Tóno gave me a stick of white chalk for Juraj.
action.Q5C.label: Draw in the lights following Juraj’s sketch
action.Q5C.001: Here, here, and these two next to each other. Thank you.
action.Q5C.002: Now it looks as if somebody really lives there.
action.Q5C.003: Exactly. It’s not just a picture of a block of flats any more.
action.Q5C.x02: Two brothers live there, and they argue across the balconies about who should switch the light on first.
action.Q5C.journal: The lights on Juraj’s panel are drawn in.
action.Q9D.001: At my first exhibition, someone told me a different design isn’t a wrong one. Since then I’ve filled a whole notebook, and I teach children to build radios.
action.Q9D.002: That notebook will get even thicker.
action.Q9D.003: You say that as if you’d already seen it.
action.Q9D.x01: A full notebook? How many schematics are in it?
action.Q9D.x02: Forty-two. But it didn’t stop at schematics. I built a radio from every one, and they all work.
action.Q9D.x03: And do the children’s radios work?
action.Q9D.x04: Almost all of them. One only picks up taxi drivers, and its owner is the happiest of the lot.
action.Q9D.journal: Jana runs a group for children in the prep room and teaches them to build radios.
action.Q11A.001: Why are you tapping that bell?
action.Q11A.002: Because it won’t ring. I tap and tap and nothing.
action.Q11A.003: Let me see. It’s missing its cap – the very part that rings.
action.Q11A.004: It popped off when I rode up on the kerb. And then it rolled away.
action.Q11A.005: It bounced three times and vanished under the blue spruce. I counted.
action.Q11A.006: I didn’t count. I was falling off.
action.Q11A.007: I saw that too. The knee survived; the bell hasn’t yet.
action.Q11A.008: At the end of the year we all go round the yard ringing our bells. Without a bell it doesn’t count.
action.Q11A.009: I’ll find the cap and screw it back on. At the end of the year, you’ll be ringing.
action.Q11A.objective: Find the cap of Kubo’s bell under the blue spruce at Pri LEALe.
action.Q11A.journal: Find the cap of Kubo’s bell under the blue spruce at Pri LEALe.
action.Q11A.hint_step: At Pri LEALe, talk to Kubo about the bell on his bike.
action.Q11B.label: Look for the cap under the spruce
action.Q11B.001: Pine needles, two bits of chalk, an old ball and a brass cap.
action.Q11B.002: It bounced three times and stopped right here. Zuzana counted well.
action.Q11B.objective: Screw the cap back onto the bell on Kubo’s bike.
action.Q11B.journal: Screw the cap back onto the bell on Kubo’s bike.
action.Q11B.hint_step: Look for the bell cap under the blue spruce at Pri LEALe.
action.Q11C.label: Screw the cap onto the bell
action.Q11C.001: Cap on the thread, a quarter turn, and tighten it gently with the screwdriver. Kubo, don’t tap yet – my fingers are in there.
action.Q11C.002: It rings! Auntie Zuzana, can you hear it?
action.Q11C.003: I can. The whole yard can.
action.Q11C.004: And now listen to this, too. They’re ringing the bell at school.
action.Q11C.005: When I hear the bell ring at the end of the year, I wave. An old agreement.
action.Q11C.007: With a man who repairs bells.
action.Q11C.008: But it isn’t the end of the year yet.
action.Q11C.009: Fifteen more days. This is a rehearsal.
action.Q11C.010: The rehearsal went well. I’m waving with you.
action.Q11C.journal: Kubo’s bell rings. Zuzana and I waved when the school bell rang.
action.Q11C.hint_step: Use the bell cap on Kubo’s bike.
entry.S11.001: My phone has no signal and the tram is in the colours of my childhood. This is no ordinary network outage.
look.S11.ambient 1: A paper timetable, with the delays added in pen. Someone here keeps their own statistics too.
look.S11.ambient 2: Chewing gum from several school years. One of them might be mine.
entry.S12.001: My school on Sokolíkova. If anyone calls me up to the blackboard, I’m returning time travel as faulty.
look.S12.ambient 1: A heavy concrete planter with one brave geranium in it. Not even the caretaker could shift that planter.
look.S12.ambient 2: The school’s coat of arms and name are where they belong. In my first year I thought the headmaster had drawn that coat of arms himself.
look.S12.notice: ‘This afternoon: Our School’s Sound Atlas. Tape recorder won’t play – a repairer’s help welcome. Report to the caretaker.’
entry.S13.001: You never forget that smell: floor polish, indoor shoes and fear of tests.
look.S13.TONO: Tóno, the young caretaker. He can tell by the sound which door has just opened.
look.S13.ambient 1: Indoor shoes lined up like an army. Mine were always at the end, because I always came last.
look.S13.ambient 2: The keys to the whole school. Whoever holds them decides where you can go.
exit.S13.to_S15.locked: The prep room is locked. First I’ll report to the caretaker and show him the chronometer.
conn.S13.S15.locked: The prep room is locked. First I’ll report to the caretaker and show him the chronometer.
entry.S14.001: Gran is fifty-five, I’m thirty-five. And I still have a feeling she’s about to send me off to wash my hands.
look.S14.LEA95: Miss Lea, the teacher, is waiting for the recording to fade out. She knows how to let a silence finish its sentence.
look.S14.MIRA95: Gran has three devices in front of her. Not one of them would dare break down near her.
look.S14.ambient 1: A green blackboard. One look at it and I feel I’ve forgotten to revise.
look.S14.ambient 2: This sponge has wiped away more wrong answers than ever made it into a school report.
entry.S15.001: The physics prep room. As a pupil I wasn’t allowed to touch anything in here. Now it’s going to be my job.
look.S15.JANA95: A young woman with a ring binder. She holds it carefully, as if her own drawings were inside.
look.S15.ambient 1: A model of an eye. It looks at me the way the physics teacher did when I didn’t know Ohm’s law.
look.S15.ambient 2: A glass prism that splits light into colours. The physics teacher used to make rainbows on the ceiling with it.
look.S15.register: Gran lent the school a box of measurement records and a tape recorder. The node map is in her collection in the reading room, with the negative next to it.
look.S15.register.variant1: The register now gives the right origin too: Z-17, from 1962. Only the record has changed; the school is still the same.
exit.S15.to_S13.locked: Locked. First I’ll report to the caretaker and show him the chronometer.
exit.S15.to_S16.locked: Locked. First I’ll report to the caretaker and show him the chronometer.
conn.S15.S16.locked: Locked. First I’ll report to the caretaker and show him the chronometer.
entry.S16.001: The school PA. The place that makes even good news sound like a telling-off.
look.S16.ambient 1: One cough into it and the whole school knew.
look.S16.ambient 2: ‘Buns tomorrow.’ The only announcement the whole school ever listened to right to the end.
look.S16.deck: The motor spins freely; the drive belt has perished. I can’t safely take the cassette out without a repair.
look.S16.deck.variant1: The mechanism works and I have the cassette. Now its tracks need reading properly.
look.S16.socket: The cassette could be played here. But the two tracks cancel each other out; a cross adaptor would reverse the polarity of one of them.
look.S16.socket.variant1: The lead stays here; the PA will find it useful. The original cassette is in my bag, where the chronometer protects it.
exit.S16.to_S15.locked: Locked. First I’ll report to the caretaker and show him the chronometer.
entry.S19.001: The man with the accordion plays slowly. The trams are his drummers.
look.S19.EMIL: Emil keeps the tempo, even when the city around him doesn’t.
look.S19.ambient 1: A battered case. It’s done more miles than most suitcases.
look.S19.ambient 2: A few crowns at the bottom. THANK YOU is handwritten on the cup.
entry.S20.001: A repair shop. Here broken things still get mended, not thrown away.
look.S20.PALI: Pali doesn’t look at the brand. He listens to what’s rattling inside.
look.S20.ambient 1: A television as deep as my entire workbench.
look.S20.ambient 2: ‘I DON’T REPAIR RELATIONSHIPS.’ And underneath, in smaller letters: ‘Or televisions after a storm.’
entry.S21.001: The city centre. Everyone is rushing somewhere. I’m the only one who’s twenty-five years late.
look.S21.ambient 1: A pigeon strolls across the square as if it held the lease. Pedestrians walk round it, not the other way round.
look.S21.ambient 2: A paper map of the city. It doesn’t need a battery, just patience when folding it.
look.S21.map: Dúbravka and Karlova Ves in the west, Staré Mesto in the middle, Ružinov in the east, Petržalka across the Danube.
entry.S25.001: Miletička market. Here I can find every component, and a stallholder who asks what I want it for.
look.S25.TRH: Fero throws in a story with every component. Free of charge.
look.S25.ambient 1: Parsley. The only thing at the market that isn’t pretending to be a brand.
look.S25.ambient 2: A faded parasol. It’s seen more sun than I have.
look.S25.scale: A washer has got stuck in the groove. I can pull it out with the pliers from my bag – no need to take the scales apart.
entry.S27.001: The club has three rules: don’t kick the speakers, don’t touch the tape, and don’t say everything hisses.
look.S27.JURO: Juro hears hiss and knows straight away what year it comes from.
look.S27.ambient 1: The poster has stayed on the wall longer than the band stayed together.
look.S27.ambient 2: An empty case, but with a catalogue number. Here even what’s missing is on record.
entry.S26.001: A tailor’s. They rescue trousers here, and wedding dresses at the last minute.
look.S26.MILADA: Milada measures first and promises afterwards. She wears her tape measure round her neck like a doctor’s stethoscope.
look.S26.ambient 1: She stands still and doesn’t want anything taken in. The ideal customer.
look.S26.ambient 2: Hundreds of buttons and no two alike. Finding a pair here would take until evening.
entry.S23.001: The reading room. People whisper, turn pages and nobody hurries. Nor will I.
look.S23.ARCHIVAR: Mr Merta has a place for every box and a box for every place.
look.S23.ambient 1: Until this stamp comes down, nothing here is valid.
look.S23.ambient 2: It’s two minutes slow. I’d set it right, but here I’d probably need a stamped application for that.
entry.S24.001: Here photos are still developed. The people in them look as if they spent ages getting ready for the picture.
look.S24.FOTO: Alena can tell at a glance whether a shot is properly exposed. I can tell whether a joint is properly soldered.
look.S24.ambient 1: A family portrait. Everyone is looking somewhere else, as if the photographer had told them to look natural.
look.S24.ambient 2: Photos drying on a line like washing. Weddings, first-years and one dog – the only one smiling.
entry.S22.001: Nothing gets thrown away here. Even the price tags have historical value.
look.S22.VIERA: Viera knows which shelf holds the thing I’m only just starting to look for.
look.S22.ambient 1: Here you literally climb a ladder to reach higher literature.
look.S22.ambient 2: A book about tidying up. It has more dust on it than anything else in the shop.
entry.S28.001: An underpass with a good echo. Even three notes would sound like a concert here.
look.S28.JURAJ: Juraj draws blocks of flats so that you can see the homes in them.
look.S28.ambient 1: Every tile is a slightly different white. Some were probably replaced one at a time.
look.S28.ambient 2: A skateboard leaning against the wall. Judging by the battered deck, someone has tried it on the stairs too.
look.S28.mural: The youth club’s approved panel, drawn on in chalk. The blocks of flats are finished, but the windows are still dark.
look.S28.mural.variant1: The lit windows have joined the blocks of flats into one neighbourhood. In the corner there’s Juraj’s signature and a little drawing of a piece of chalk.
entry.S29.001: Garage number seventeen. Instead of a car there’s a transmitter, and more cables than in my workshop.
look.S29.DEZI: Dezider has a label on every cable. Even the one that goes nowhere: NOWHERE.
look.S29.ambient 1: With this aerial Dezider can reach further than I can on my mobile.
look.S29.ambient 2: A cable hangs over the back of the chair. Here the chair doubles as a coat hook.
entry.S17.001: That’s probably me in that window, aged ten. Luckily I’m looking the other way, like in every photo.
look.S17.SONA: Soňa keeps her album better organised than I keep my accounts.
look.S17.ambient 1: The net is missing. The points are counted by whoever shouts loudest anyway.
look.S17.ambient 2: At the edge of the yard there’s a weak, scraped little tree. By 2020 it will be gone.
look.S17.ambient 2.variant1: The lime we protected in 1982 already has a sturdy young crown. All it took was diverting one handcart.
look.S17.rhythm: The club’s art panel: a circle, a triangle, a square and a purple V. I know three of those shapes from Gran’s workshop.
entry.S30.001: The Danube flows the way it should. Of the two of us, I’m the one travelling strangely.
look.S30.ambient 1: A cargo boat heading upstream. The captain is drying his washing on deck and is in no hurry at all.
look.S30.ambient 2: That stays between me and the Danube.
look.S30.coil: A round holder for Dezider’s measuring coil. It has a notch, so I can’t put it in the wrong way round.
look.S30.dial: Three dials: 0–9. Gran wrote the label: ‘Digits – the drawing at Pri LEALe.’ The node map and the tape are needed too.
look.S30.metro: A little table with a mark for the metronome. Here the rhythm mustn’t depend on electricity.
entry.S18.001: The kiosk sells newspapers, chewing gum and news that isn’t in the newspapers yet.
look.S18.ZITA: Zita could publish a local paper from memory.
look.S18.ambient 1: Chewing gum wrappers with pictures. Once I’d have swapped anything for them.
look.S18.ambient 2: Nothing about time travel on the front page. So far I’m being discreet.
entry.S69.001: Pri LEALe. I once kicked a ball over the wall here and looked for it until dark.
look.S69.KUBO: A little boy with a grazed knee is tapping the bell on his bike. The bell stays silent.
look.S69.KUBO.variant1: Kubo circles the playground, ringing at every bend. Even where there isn’t one.
look.S69.ZUZANA95: A woman with a piece of chalk in her hand is studying me as if she knew me from somewhere. I don’t know her. I think.
look.S69.ZUZANA95.variant1: Zuzana, from the park in Ivanka. For her, thirty-three years have passed; for me, a lot less.
look.S69.bench: A green bench, freshly painted. Probably the one they complain about at the kiosk.
look.S69.bike: A small bike with stabilisers. The bell is missing its cap; only the bare thread sticks out.
look.S69.bike.variant1: Kubo’s bike. The bell has its cap back and rings at every bump.
look.S69.birch: A birch behind the wall. White bark, thin branches and leaves that tremble even when there’s no wind at all.
look.S69.court: A hopscotch drawn in chalk: eight squares and a half-circle at the top. The lines are straighter than in my drawings.
look.S69.gap: A narrow passage between the blocks. It leads to more entrances and more walls.
look.S69.lamp: A globe lamp. When it comes on in the evening, the children know it’s time to go home. You can hide a watch; you can’t hide a lamp.
look.S69.rhythm: A circle, a triangle, a square, a purple V, and below them THREE WAVES, TWO BEATS, SIX SEGMENTS. That’s the setting 3–2–6.
look.S69.spruce: A blue spruce, prickly on every side. That’s where balls and chalk end up. Nobody likes putting their hand in there.
look.S69.spruce.variant1: Something is glinting among the needles under the spruce. Something brass.
look.S69.spruce.variant2: Under the spruce there are only needles left, and one forgotten piece of chalk.
look.S69.wall: A wall of concrete panels standing on end. The ball never bounces off it where I aim it.
topic.ARCHIVAR.ambient 1.label: How long do you keep things?
topic.ARCHIVAR.ambient 1.002: And when the value only shows later?
topic.ARCHIVAR.ambient 1.003: That’s why I never throw anything away prematurely.
topic.ARCHIVAR.ambient 1.x01: And when is the right time?
topic.ARCHIVAR.ambient 1.x02: It hasn’t come yet. The reading room is twenty-two years old, and the bin is still new.
topic.ARCHIVAR.ambient 2.label: The quiet in the reading room
topic.ARCHIVAR.ambient 2.002: Please don’t comment on it out loud.
topic.ARCHIVAR.ambient 2.x02: Whispering, yes. Sighing over your notes, no. That’s the most disturbing thing of all.
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 1.label: The strangest donation
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 1.001: What’s the strangest thing anyone has ever donated to you?
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 1.002: A box of buttons and a note: ‘From the coats of our street, 1948 to 1990.’
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 1.004: Every button separately. It took the whole winter.
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 1.005: What does an archive want with a box of buttons?
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 1.006: Buttons tell you what coats people wore on our street. You won’t find that in any document.
